title: Gasoline and Gasoline-Ethanol Fuel-System Safety
introduction: I start fuel-system work by separating stored pressure from ignition hazards. Stopping the engine does not remove the first, and spilled fuel can meet the second when the engine is restarted. These precautions explain what must be controlled before and during work. They accompany the applicable service procedure; they do not provide the pressure-relief method, battery-disconnection procedure or a complete fuel-system repair sequence.

items.name: Fuel filler cap, where fitted
items.detail: Remove the fuel filler cap slowly. If it vents vapor or you hear hissing, wait until that stops before removing it completely. Pressure can otherwise spray fuel out and cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Running-engine visual leak inspection
items.detail: Avoid fuel contact during a visual leak inspection with the engine running. Do not work on the fuel system until pressure has been released and the engine has cooled. High-pressure fuel is hot and under very high pressure: it can cause cuts, and hot fuel can cause burns. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury.

edits.text: WARNING: Relieve fuel-system pressure before working on or disconnecting any fuel tube or fuel-system component to prevent accidental fuel spray. Fuel remains under high pressure even when the engine is not running. Failure to follow this instruction may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: An engine that has stopped can still contain pressurized fuel. Use the applicable pressure-relief procedure before opening the system; switching the engine off does not establish that pressure has been released.

edits.text: WARNING: Do not smoke, carry lighted tobacco or allow any open flame while working on or near a fuel-related component. Highly flammable mixtures are always present and may ignite. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: The ignition-source restriction applies near the components as well as during direct work on them.

edits.text: WARNING: Remove all fuel residue from the engine compartment. Residue left behind may ignite when the engine is returned to operation. Failure to follow this instruction may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: Cleanup is a condition for returning the engine to operation, not merely a matter of leaving the work area tidy.

edits.text: WARNING: Do not carry personal electronic devices, including cell phones, pagers or audio equipment of any type, while working on or near a fuel-related component. Highly flammable mixtures are always present and may ignite. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: This restriction belongs to the ignition-hazard precautions and applies throughout the work near fuel-related components.

edits.text: WARNING: Always disconnect the battery ground cable at the battery when working on an evaporative emission (EVAP) system or a fuel-related component. Highly flammable mixtures are always present and may ignite. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: The requirement covers vapor-system work as well as other fuel-related work. EVAP contains and manages fuel vapor, so the ignition precautions remain relevant even when the component is not a liquid-fuel supply line.

edits.text: WARNING: Always observe fuel-handling precautions and prepare for possible spillage whenever handling fuel. Hot vehicle components or other ignition sources can ignite spilled fuel. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: Spill preparation belongs before fuel handling begins. Hot components remain a potential ignition source alongside the other sources addressed by these warnings.

edits.text: WARNING: Loosen and remove the fuel filler cap slowly because the fuel system may be pressurized. If vapor vents from the cap or you hear hissing, pause until the venting or hissing stops before removing the cap completely. Removing it too soon can allow fuel to spray out. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: The escaping vapor or hissing is the observable signal to wait. I use that signal to decide when to continue opening the cap; it does not replace the required fuel-system pressure-release procedure before working on fuel tubes or components.

edits.text: WARNING: During a visual check for fuel leaks with the engine running, avoid all contact with fuel. Before working on the fuel system, release its pressure and allow the engine to cool. Fuel in the high-pressure fuel system is hot and under very high pressure: high-pressure fuel can cause cuts, and hot fuel can cause burns. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: Looking for a leak with the engine running does not authorize hands-on fuel-system work. Both pressure release and engine cooling are required before that work begins. Switching the engine off alone is insufficient because fuel pressure can remain.
